newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas mostly turns up late, support holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas mostly turns up late, support holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly turned higher late Tuesday in still-quiet post-bidweek trade, helped by some technical buying when downside momentum stalled early in the session, sources said.
But they noted prices remained in recent technical ranges, with many sidelined waiting for clearer signs from the cash once May flows begin on Thursday.

At 1415 EDT, May climbed 3.4 cents to $2.115 per million British thermal units after an early move down stalled at $2.055, just above support. June was 1.4 cents higher at $2.12. Most other deferreds were steady to up slightly.

With mostly seasonal weather forecast this week for much of the nation, some expected May to open on a soft note, pointing to a lack of cooling demand in the South and the loss of recent heating loads in the Midwest and Northeast.
Early estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA inventory report range from a draw of 10 bcf to a build of 30 bcf.

Technical traders agreed the market was still range-bound, but some said a break below $2 (basis June) could trigger a flood of liquidation, noting funds and speculators have been big buyers recently.
In the meantime, they pegged next support in June at $2.03, which coincides with short-term trendline support now in the low-$2s. Resistance was seen at $2.18, $2.24 and then at $2.33.

In the May cash, Gulf Coast prices notionally were little changed in the $2.04-09 range. May Midcon pipes slipped a couple of cents to the low-$1.90s. New York city gate gas for May was several cents lower in the mid-to-high $2.30s on milder weather in the region.
NYMEX said 17,894 Hub contracts traded at 1355 EDT.
On KCBT, June firmed 1.5 cents to $1.95, while deferreds were steady to one cent lower. The East/West spread widened by 1.9 cents to 16.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
